The '''1939 Rocky Mountain Conference football season''' was the season of [[college football]] played by the five member schools of the [[Rocky Mountain Conference]] (RMC) as part of the [[1939 college football season]].

The [[1939 Colorado Mines Orediggers football team|Colorado Mines Orediggers]], led by head coach [[John Mason (American football)|John Mason]], compiled a perfect 8–0 record and won the RMC championship. They led the RMC in both scoring offense (33.5 points per game) and scoring defense (8.8 points per game). Colorado Mines wingback Lloyd Madden led the nation with 143 points scored.

The '''1939 Colorado Mines Orediggers football team''' represented the [[Colorado School of Mines]] of [[Golden, Colorado]]. In their third year under head coach [[John Mason (American football)|John Mason]], the Orediggers compiled a perfect 8–0 record, outscored opponents by a total of 268 to 44, and won the RMC championship.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.cfbdatawarehouse.com/data/active/c/colorado_mines/1935-1939_yearly_results.php|title=Colorado School of Mines Yearly Results|publisher=College Football Data Warehouse|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150907060644/http://www.cfbdatawarehouse.com/data/active/c/colorado_mines/1935-1939_yearly_results.php|access-date=October 24, 2021|archive-date=2015-09-07}}</ref>

Colorado Mines was ranked at No. 93 (out of 609 teams) in the final [[Litkenhous Ratings]] for 1939.<ref name="E. E. Litkenhous 11">{{cite news|title=Vols Second In Final Litkenhous Grid Rankings; Southern California Tenth|author=E. E. Litkenhous|newspaper=Johnson City Sunday Press|date=December 31, 1939|page=11|url=https://www.newspapers.com/clip/123000367/vols-second-in-final-litkenhous-grid/|via=[[Newspapers.com]]}}</ref>

Colorado Mines wingback Lloyd Madden won the national scoring title with 141 points scored (23 touchdowns and three extra points).<ref>{{cite news|title=Colorado Mines Grid Star Takes National Scoring Leadership|newspaper=Rapid City Journal|date=December 4, 1939|page=7|url=https://www.newspapers.com/clip/87950712/colorado-mines-grid-star-takes-national/|via=[[Newspapers.com]]}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|title=Miners Want Another Game: Seek Invitation to a Bowl Contest|newspaper=Casper Star-Tribune|date=December 4, 1939|page=4|url=https://www.newspapers.com/clip/87950506/miners-want-another-game-seek/|via=[[Newspapers.com]]}}</ref> He broke the RMC scoring record set in 1937 by [[Byron White]].<ref name=CMDR/> He was selected by the [[Chicago Cardinals]] with the 16th overall pick in the [[1940 NFL draft]].<ref name=PFR>{{cite web|title=Lloyd Madden Stats|publisher=Sports Reference LLC|work=Pro-Football-Reference.com|access-date=March 21, 2021|url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/M/MaddLl20.htm}}</ref>

Colorado Mines secured eight of eleven first-team spots on the [[Associated Press]] All-Rocky Mountain Conference football team.<ref name=AP>{{cite news|title=A.P. All-Conference|newspaper=Greeley Daily Tribune|date=December 4, 1939|page=7|url=https://www.newspapers.com/clip/87943657/ap-all-conference-team/|via=[[Newspapers.com]]}}</ref> Six were also given first-team conference honors by the [[United Press]].<ref name=UP>{{cite news|title=Funk Selected All-Conference End For Second Time|newspaper=Greeley Daily Tribune|date=December 4, 1939|page=7|url=https://www.newspapers.com/clip/87943845/funk-selected-all-conference-end-for/|via=[[Newspapers.com]]}}</ref> The first-team honorees were: backs Madden (AP-1, UP-1), Joe Berta (AP-1), Jacky Torpey (AP-1, UP-1), and Taylor (UP-1); end Rex Flynn (AP-1, UP-1); tackles Marv Katzenstein (AP-1, UP-1) and Dick Moe (AP-1, UP-1); guard Dave Geiskieng (AP-1, UP-1); and center Herbert Thornton (AP-1).<ref name=AP/><ref name=UP/>

The '''1939 Colorado State–Greeley Bears football team''' represented Colorado State College at [[Greeley, Colorado]] (now known as the [[University of Northern Colorado]]). In their eighth year under head coach [[John W. Hancock]], the Bears compiled a 4–4 record (3–1 against RMC opponents) and finished in second place out of five teams in the RMC.

Colorado State–Greeley was ranked at No. 225 (out of 609 teams) in the final [[Litkenhous Ratings]] for 1939.<ref name="E. E. Litkenhous 11"/>

The team played its home games at Jackson Field in [[Greeley, Colorado]].
